items.stem: A live-captioning feature must show words as the speaker talks. Which transcription mode fits, and why?

options.text: Streaming transcription, because it emits partial results continuously with low latency instead of waiting for the full audio
options.rationale: Correct: live captions need incremental, low-latency output that streaming provides.

options.text: Batch transcription, because it is always more accurate
options.rationale: Batch waits for the whole file and cannot caption live, regardless of accuracy.
Captions are text from speech; that is STT, not TTS.

items.explanation: Correct: live captions need incremental, low-latency output that streaming provides.

items.stem: Which TWO factors most affect speech-to-text word error rate in production? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Domain-specific or rare vocabulary the model was not tuned for
options.rationale: Correct: unusual terms raise error rates unless the model adapts.

options.text: The colour of the user interface
options.rationale: UI colour is irrelevant to transcription accuracy.

options.text: Whether the transcript is displayed in bold
options.rationale: Display styling does not affect recognition accuracy.

items.stem: Why add pronunciation markup to a text-to-speech request for a product named 'Xyla'?

options.text: To tell the synthesiser how to pronounce an unusual name the default voice would likely mispronounce
options.rationale: Correct: markup controls pronunciation of names and terms the model cannot infer.

options.text: To translate the name into another language

options.rationale: That is STT; markup here is for synthesis.

options.text: To reduce the audio sample rate
options.rationale: Pronunciation markup does not change sample rate.

items.explanation: Correct: markup controls pronunciation of names and terms the model cannot infer.
